name: Andreessen Horowitz

summary.text: Andreessen Horowitz launched in July 2009 with a $300 million fund and in January 2026 was reported to have raised more than $15 billion in new funds. It committed $400 million to Elon Musk's 2022 Twitter purchase. It has co-invested with Peter Thiel's Founders Fund (Affirm) and with Sequoia Capital (Twitter purchase, xAI). It is among the largest donors to the crypto super PAC Fairshake and helped launch the AI super PAC network Leading the Future in 2025. Its in-house lobbying reports total $3.53 million for 2025. Former partners Scott Kupor (OPM director) and Sriram Krishnan (White House AI policy adviser) took posts in the 2025 Trump administration.

facts.claim: FEC filings show that AH Capital Management, Andreessen Horowitz's management company, contributed $67 million to the Fairshake super PAC between October 2023 and November 2024, attributed in memo entries equally to Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. It contributed a further $23.8 million in December 2025.

sources.title: Individual contributions to Fairshake from AH Capital Management

facts.claim: On October 16, 2023, Marc Andreessen published 'The Techno-Optimist Manifesto' on a16z's website. It states that 'any deceleration of AI will cost lives' and that 'Deaths that were preventable by the AI that was prevented from existing is a form of murder.' It also names ideas including 'existential risk', 'trust and safety', 'tech ethics' and the 'Precautionary Principle' as 'enemies', and states 'Our enemy is deceleration'.

sources.title: The Techno-Optimist Manifesto

facts.claim: Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz launched Andreessen Horowitz with a $300 million venture fund on the evening of July 5–6, 2009, saying it would invest $50,000 to $50 million per company, generally at early stage. The report named no limited partners.

sources.title: Details on Marc Andreessen's New Fund (Plus Five Other Interesting Things He Said)

facts.claim: Andreessen Horowitz led Airbnb's $112 million Series B in July 2011, reportedly putting in about $60 million, alongside DST ($40 million) and General Catalyst. Airbnb's earlier $7.8 million Series A investors included Greylock and Sequoia Capital.

sources.title: Airbnb Bags $112 Million In Series B From Andreessen, DST And General Catalyst

facts.claim: Fortune reported, citing California lobbying records, that a16z raised $400 million from CalPERS, the state's public employees' pension fund, for a new fund called California Innovation Opportunities. a16z's head of investor relations registered as a California lobbyist to seek investment from CalPERS, CalSTRS and the University of California Regents.

sources.title: Andreessen Horowitz is adding major California pension funds to its LP base for the first time, records show

facts.claim: On January 9, 2026, a16z's law firm Cooley announced that a16z had raised more than $15 billion for new funds: Growth ($6.75 billion), Apps ($1.7 billion), Infrastructure ($1.7 billion), American Dynamism ($1.176 billion), Bio + Health ($700 million) and other venture strategies ($3 billion). Its previous raise closed at $7.2 billion for five funds in April 2024.

sources.title: Andreessen Horowitz Raises More Than $15 Billion in New Funds

facts.claim: The pro-AI super PAC network Leading the Future launched in August 2025 with $100 million in backing from Andreessen Horowitz and OpenAI president Greg Brockman, with Joe Lonsdale, Ron Conway and Perplexity also named as supporters. It said it would start in New York, California, Illinois and Ohio, and Fortune noted it hoped to repeat the success of Fairshake.

sources.title: OpenAI's president and Andreessen Horowitz are helping lead a $100 million Silicon Valley push against tougher AI laws

facts.claim: Andreessen Horowitz reported $950,000 in federal lobbying in 2023 and $1.8 million in 2024, focused on digital-asset regulation, stablecoins, AI and defense, narrowly outspending the National Venture Capital Association in the first half of 2025.

sources.title: a16z spends $1.49M in Washington lobbying, while rivals mostly sit out

facts.claim: A16Z Capital Management's in-house lobbying reports for 2025 list expenses of $650,000 (Q1), $840,000 (Q2, as amended), $1,330,000 (Q3) and $710,000 (Q4), $3.53 million in total. The Q1 report covered digital assets and market structure, anti-money laundering, AI, health, the FY2026 NDAA and tax.

sources.title: A16Z Capital Management LLC in-house LD-2 reports, 2025

facts.claim: In Q1 2025, outside firms Miller Strategies, LLC and BGR Government Affairs registered to lobby for A16Z Capital Management on AI and digital-asset market structure, reporting Q1 income of $50,000 and $30,000 respectively.

sources.title: Filings for client A16Z / AH Capital Management, 2025

facts.claim: On December 22, 2024, President-elect Trump named Scott Kupor, described as Andreessen Horowitz's first employee and a managing partner, to lead the Office of Personnel Management. The Senate confirmed him 49–46 on July 9, 2025.

sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara)

facts.claim: On December 22, 2024, Trump named Sriram Krishnan, most recently a partner at Andreessen Horowitz, as Senior Policy Advisor for AI at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, to work closely with AI and crypto czar David Sacks. TechCrunch reported in June 2026 that Krishnan would leave the post at the end of that month.

connections.claim: Andreessen Horowitz invested in Affirm, the lender founded and run by Max Levchin, joining as a new investor in its $275 million debt-and-equity round in May 2015 and investing again in Affirm's $100 million round led by Founders Fund in April 2016.

connections.claim: When Marc Andreessen (who co-founded a16z in 2009) joined Facebook's board in June 2008, the board was Mark Zuckerberg, Jim Breyer (Accel) and Peter Thiel (Clarium Capital and Founders Fund), with David Sze of Greylock Partners as a board observer.

sources.title: Marc Andreessen Joins Facebook Board of Directors

openQuestions: No specific deal found with sources where a16z co-invested alongside Craft Ventures/David Sacks, Keith Rabois, or Reid Hoffman personally; Greylock and a16z shared Airbnb only across different rounds.
Limited partners: apart from the reported CalPERS $400 million commitment (2023), no LP list found; whether CalSTRS or UC Regents invested is unconfirmed.
Leading the Future's combined figure with affiliates ($125 million in 2025 per NOTUS) includes commitments and its 501(c)(4); only the super PAC's own FEC receipts were verified.
Full-year 2025 lobbying by outside firms (Miller Strategies, BGR and others) was not totalled; only in-house LD-2 expenses were summed.
Reports of a 2026 Anduril round led by a16z with a large Founders Fund check came only from aggregators and were not verified.
The CJR-cited Andreessen text to Musk is from secondary coverage of Delaware Chancery exhibits, not the exhibit itself.
